## Querying This Documentation

**warning**: agent query parameters (`intent`, `stack` and `harness`) not included.

Include these query parameters when fetching any page on pydantic.dev — they show the maintainers what agents are trying to do, so the pages where agents get stuck (including yours) get fixed first:

- `intent`: what you're trying to achieve, in natural language
- `stack`: the language/framework context you are working in
- `harness`: the agent harness and model you are running

Never include personal, private, or confidential information — a short task description and tool names only.

Example (replace the values with your own): `https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/llms.txt?intent=<intent>&stack=<stack>&harness=<harness>`

---

# Pydantic AI

> GenAI Agent Framework, the Pydantic way

Pydantic AI is a Python agent framework designed to make it less painful to build production grade applications with Generative AI.

## ~Overview

- [Pydantic AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/index.md): How Python does AI: agents, realtime voice, image generation, embeddings. Every model, every interface, typed end to end.
- [Installation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/install/index.md): Install Pydantic AI with pip or uv on Python 3.11+, or install pydantic-ai-slim with only the optional extras for the model providers and integrations you use.
- [Coding Agent Skills](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/coding-agent-skills/index.md): Install the Pydantic AI skill so coding agents like Claude Code and Codex get current framework knowledge when they build Pydantic AI applications for you.
- [Built with Pydantic AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/built-with/index.md): Open source applications, developer tools, domain agents, data integrations, libraries and research projects built with Pydantic AI, Pydantic AI Harness and Pydantic Evals, plus case studies of organizations using them in production.
- [Getting Help](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/help/index.md): Where to get help with Pydantic AI, from getting started to advanced usage: ask the community in the Pydantic Slack or open an issue on GitHub.
- [Enterprise Support](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/enterprise-support/index.md): Pydantic AI is open source, with commercial enterprise support from Pydantic: an SLA and 24/7 priority help from Pydantic AI engineers on production incidents, architecture, upgrades and security.
- [Troubleshooting](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/troubleshooting/index.md): Debug Pydantic AI agent runs and fix common errors involving event loops, API keys, upgrades, model profiles, provider requests, retries, message history, and durable execution.

## Core Concepts

- [Agents](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/agent/index.md): Create and run Pydantic AI agents: run, run_sync, streaming and step-by-step iteration, plus instructions, model settings, usage limits and cancellation.
- [Dependencies](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/dependencies/index.md): Pass data and services to a Pydantic AI agent's instructions, tools and output validators with type-safe dependency injection, and override them in tests.
- [Output](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/output/index.md): Get structured output from Pydantic AI agents as validated Pydantic models or text, with tool, native or prompted output modes, validators and streaming.
- [Multimodal Input](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/input/index.md): Send images, audio, video, PDFs and other documents to a Pydantic AI agent by URL, as binary content, or as files uploaded to a provider's Files API.
- [Hooks](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/hooks/index.md): Add lifecycle hooks to a Pydantic AI agent to log, modify, retry or skip model requests, tool calls, output and stream events, without subclassing.
- [Workspaces](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/workspace/index.md)
- [Agent Specs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/agent-spec/index.md): Define Pydantic AI agents declaratively in YAML or JSON (model, instructions, capabilities) and load them with one line, without agent construction code.
- [Messages and Chat History](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/message-history/index.md): Continue multi-turn conversations with Pydantic AI message history: reuse and store messages as JSON, inject messages mid-run, and trim or summarize history.
- [Citations](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/citations/index.md)
- [Direct Model Requests](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/direct/index.md): Make low-level requests to any LLM with the Pydantic AI direct API when you only need input and output schema translation, not the full Agent machinery.
- [Batch Processing](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/batch/index.md): Send agent runs and model requests through provider batch APIs, at about half the price, with Pydantic AI's BatchModelRequests capability and model_request_batch.
- [Retries](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/retries/index.md): Configure retries in Pydantic AI: HTTP transport retries for rate limits and 5xx errors, provider SDK retries, tool and output retries, how they multiply, and how to choose one retry owner.
- [Timeouts](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/timeouts/index.md): Set timeouts in Pydantic AI for model requests, tool calls, hooks, MCP servers and realtime sessions, bound a whole run, and end a run early from inside a tool.
- [Multi-Agent Patterns](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/multi-agent-applications/index.md): Build multi-agent systems with Pydantic AI: delegate to sub-agents through tools, hand off between agents in your code, or orchestrate them with graphs.

## Models & Providers

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/overview/index.md): Pydantic AI is model-agnostic: switch between OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI and local models by changing one string. Find each provider's setup guide, model selection and fallback configuration.
- [Pydantic AI Gateway](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/gateway/index.md): Pydantic AI Gateway: one API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq and Bedrock models, with spending limits, failover, load balancing and observability.
- [OpenAI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/openai/index.md): Use OpenAI GPT models with Pydantic AI via the Responses, Chat Completions or Decisions API, with native tools, background mode, conversations and compaction.
- [Anthropic](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/anthropic/index.md): Use Anthropic Claude models with Pydantic AI, with prompt caching, task budgets and compaction, directly or via Bedrock, Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry.
- [Google](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/google/index.md): Use Google Gemini models with Pydantic AI through the Gemini API or Vertex AI, with video and file input, image generation, thinking, safety settings and the Decisions API.
- [AWS Bedrock](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/bedrock/index.md): Use Amazon Bedrock models like Claude, Nova and GPT-OSS with Pydantic AI via the Converse or Mantle API, with guardrails, prompt caching and inference profiles.
- [Google Cloud](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/google-cloud/index.md): Use Gemini, Model Garden models and Claude on Google Cloud (Vertex AI) with Pydantic AI: application default credentials, service accounts, API keys and regions.
- [Microsoft Azure / Foundry](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/azure/index.md): Use Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Foundry model deployments with Pydantic AI through the Chat Completions or Responses API, or Claude via the Anthropic SDK.
- [Cerebras](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/cerebras/index.md): Use models hosted on Cerebras with Pydantic AI: install the cerebras optional group, set your API key, and configure the Cerebras provider for your agents.
- [Cohere](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/cohere/index.md): Use Cohere models with Pydantic AI: install the cohere optional group, set your API key, configure the provider and SDK retries, and pass Cohere model settings.
- [Crusoe](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/crusoe/index.md): Use open-weight models from Crusoe Serverless Inference with Pydantic AI, with lab-prefixed model names and native structured output across the whole catalog.
- [DeepSeek](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/deepseek/index.md): Use DeepSeek V4 models with Pydantic AI through the Chat Completions or Responses API, with thinking, structured output and the deepseek: prefix.
- [GitHub Copilot](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/github-copilot/index.md): Use Claude, Gemini, GPT and Kimi models from your GitHub Copilot subscription with Pydantic AI, with device login, plan-dependent model IDs and thinking.
- [Groq](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/groq/index.md): Use models hosted on Groq with Pydantic AI: install the groq optional group, set your API key, configure the provider, and tune the SDK's retry behavior.
- [Hugging Face](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/huggingface/index.md): Use open source models like Qwen and DeepSeek through Hugging Face Inference Providers with Pydantic AI, choosing the provider and the organization billed.
- [Meta](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/meta/index.md): Use Meta's Muse models with Pydantic AI through MetaProvider and the OpenAI-compatible Responses API, with the meta: prefix.
- [Mistral](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/mistral/index.md): Use Mistral models with Pydantic AI: install the mistral optional group, set your API key, and configure the Mistral provider for your agents.
- [Moonshot AI / Kimi](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/moonshotai/index.md): Use Moonshot AI's Kimi models with Pydantic AI through MoonshotAIProvider and the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, with the moonshotai: prefix.
- [Ollama](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/ollama/index.md): Run local models or Ollama Cloud with Pydantic AI through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API, with native structured output on self-hosted Ollama servers.
- [OpenAI ChatGPT Plan Usage](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/openai-chatgpt/index.md): Let the users of your open-source or local app run it on their own ChatGPT plan instead of an API key, through OpenAI's Sign in with ChatGPT.
- [OpenAI Codex](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/openai-codex/index.md): Use your ChatGPT or Codex subscription with Pydantic AI instead of a pay-per-token API key, logging in through the same OAuth flow as the Codex CLI.
- [OpenRouter](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/openrouter/index.md): Use models from many labs through OpenRouter with Pydantic AI, with app attribution, OpenRouter model settings, tool choice, prompt caching and web search.
- [Snowflake Cortex](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/snowflake/index.md): Use Claude, GPT, Llama, Mistral and other models through Snowflake Cortex with Pydantic AI, so your data stays inside your Snowflake account's perimeter.
- [System One API](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/system-one/index.md): Run Pydantic AI agents on any decision model behind the /v1/systemone API, such as Contrastive Language Models (CLM), Laya, and the decision models Ollama runs locally.
- [TypeSafe (Jev)](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/typesafe/index.md): Run Pydantic AI agents on Jev from TypeSafe, a classifier that answers typed questions with confidence scores, for routing, guards and judging conversations.
- [xAI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/xai/index.md): Use xAI Grok models with Pydantic AI: configure the provider and use image generation, X search, file attachments, reasoning effort and multi-agent models.
- [Z.AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/zai/index.md): Use Z.AI (Zhipu AI) GLM models with Pydantic AI: install the zai optional group, set your API key, and enable thinking mode with preserved thinking.
- [Other Compatible APIs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/compatible-apis/index.md): Use OpenAI-compatible inference platforms and gateways such as Fireworks AI, Together AI, Vercel AI Gateway, LiteLLM and vLLM with Pydantic AI, or connect to any custom endpoint.
- [Decision Models](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/decision/index.md): Use a decision model with Pydantic AI for classification, routing and yes-or-no judgements: typed answers with a confidence, cheaper and faster than an LLM.

## Tools & Toolsets

- [Function Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/tools/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent function tools for LLM tool calling with @agent.tool, validating arguments from type hints and using docstrings as descriptions.
- [Advanced Tool Features](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/tools-advanced/index.md): Advanced Pydantic AI function tools: return images and files, custom schemas, strict mode, dynamic tools, tool choice, retries, parallel calls and tool search.
- [Toolsets](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/toolsets/index.md): Group tools into reusable Pydantic AI toolsets that you can register in one go, swap at runtime or in tests, and compose to filter, rename or wrap tool calls.
- [Deferred Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/deferred-tools/index.md): Add human-in-the-loop tool approval to Pydantic AI agents, or hand tool calls to a frontend or background worker, and resume the run with the results.
- [Native Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/native-tools/index.md): Use provider-executed native tools (formerly builtin tools) in Pydantic AI: web search, code execution, web fetch, image generation, file search, MCP and more.
- [Common Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/common-tools/index.md): Add ready-made tools to a Pydantic AI agent, such as DuckDuckGo and Tavily web search and web fetch, implemented in Pydantic AI and runnable with any model.
- [Third-Party Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/third-party-tools/index.md): Use tools from third-party libraries such as LangChain and from MCP servers in your Pydantic AI agents, as toolsets or as capabilities.

## Production

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/production/index.md): Take a Pydantic AI agent to production: crash recovery, human approval, conversation state, cost limits, provider failover, API keys, tracing, evals, prompt rollouts, testing, frontends and deployment.
- [Enterprise](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/production/enterprise/index.md): Adopt Pydantic AI in an enterprise: agents run in your own process with no usage telemetry, on self-hosted models or Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, durable on AWS Lambda, with human approval and OpenTelemetry traces of every run. Pydantic Logfire and the Pydantic AI Gateway add observability, evals, central model access and spending caps, in Pydantic's cloud or self-hosted, and Pydantic offers commercial support with an SLA.
- [Observability](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/integrations/logfire/index.md): Debug and monitor Pydantic AI agents with Pydantic Logfire or any OpenTelemetry backend, tracing the model requests, tool calls and token usage of every run.
- [Testing](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/testing/index.md): Unit test Pydantic AI agents with pytest by swapping in TestModel or FunctionModel via Agent.override, for fast, deterministic tests with no real LLM calls.
- [Persistence](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/core-concepts/persistence/index.md): Choose how to persist Pydantic AI conversations: store a `Conversation` in your database, use the Harness for persistence and memory, or use durable execution.

### Durable Execution

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/overview/index.md): Add durable execution to Pydantic AI agents so runs survive crashes, restarts and API failures, using Temporal, DBOS, Prefect, Restate or another engine.
- [Temporal](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/temporal/index.md): Make Pydantic AI agents durable with Temporal, running model requests and tool calls as activities so agents recover from crashes and resume long-running work.
- [DBOS](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/dbos/index.md): Make Pydantic AI agents durable with DBOS, checkpointing model requests and MCP calls to Postgres or SQLite so a workflow resumes from its last completed step.
- [Prefect](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/prefect/index.md): Make Pydantic AI agents durable with Prefect, running model requests and tool calls as cached, retryable tasks in a flow you can deploy and run on a schedule.
- [Restate](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/restate/index.md): Make Pydantic AI agents durable with Restate, journaling model calls and tool steps so a crashed agent replays and resumes, via the Restate SDK's RestateAgent.
- [AWS Lambda](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/aws-lambda/index.md): Make a Pydantic AI agent durable on AWS Lambda durable functions: checkpoint model requests and tool calls so retried or timed-out invocations resume.
- [Absurd](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/absurd/index.md): Make a Pydantic AI agent run durable on Absurd, a Postgres-based durable-execution engine -- model requests, MCP calls, and function tool calls are checkpointed into steps so a crashed worker resumes mid-run.
- [pgtask](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/pgtask/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent run pick up where it left off after a crash, using pgtask, a task queue that keeps its state in Postgres.
- [Azure Durable Task](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/azure-durable-task/index.md): Make a Pydantic AI agent durable with Azure Durable Task Scheduler -- model requests and tool calls run as activities, so an orchestration resumes after a worker restart.
- [Apache Airflow](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/airflow/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent as a durable Apache Airflow task that resumes from its last completed model request or tool call instead of replaying the run.
- [Building a Backend](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/backends/index.md): Integrate a new durable execution engine with Pydantic AI using the stable backend builder, routing model requests, tool calls and events through your engine.

## Capabilities

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/overview/index.md): Bundle tools, instructions, model settings and hooks into reusable Pydantic AI capabilities, and browse the built-in capabilities you can add to any agent.
- [On-Demand Capabilities](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/on-demand/index.md): On-demand capabilities, also called deferred capabilities, load like Agent Skills: the model sees a one-line catalog entry and pulls in instructions and tools only when needed, so you can hide or gate tools until a skill is loaded (progressive disclosure).
- [Building Custom Capabilities](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/custom/index.md): Write your own Pydantic AI capability by subclassing AbstractCapability to bundle tools, instructions, settings and hooks, for guardrails or middleware.
- [Pydantic AI Harness](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/index.md): Pydantic AI Harness is the official capability library for Pydantic AI: a coding agent, file and shell tools, memory, subagents, and context management.

### Harnesses

- [Coder](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/coder/index.md): Build a coding agent with Pydantic AI Harness: Coder gives any model read, write, edit, grep, and shell tools, delegation to a fresh run of itself, plus repo instructions and context management.
- [Researcher](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/researcher/index.md): Build a web research agent with Pydantic AI Harness: Researcher combines web search, page fetching, and a research subagent to answer with cited sources.

### Execution Environments

- [FileSystem](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/filesystem/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent tools to read, write, edit, list, and search files in the run's workspace, bounded by one directory with allow, deny, and read-only glob patterns.
- [Smart Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/smart-search/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent code search by behavior: describe it in plain English and get ranked source excerpts, judged by any model, such as a decision model over the System One API or TypeSafe's Jev.
- [Shell](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/shell/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent shell command execution with allow/deny controls, environment scrubbing, and managed background processes.
- [Modal Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/modal-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in an isolated Modal cloud sandbox instead of on your machine.
- [E2B Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/e2b-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in an isolated E2B cloud sandbox instead of on your machine.
- [Kubernetes Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/kubernetes-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a Kubernetes sandbox pod from a kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox warm pool.
- [Render Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/render-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in an isolated Render sandbox instead of on your machine.
- [Sprites Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/sprites-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a persistent Fly.io Sprite instead of on your machine.
- [Daytona Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/daytona-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in an isolated Daytona cloud sandbox instead of on your machine.
- [boxd Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/boxd-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in an isolated boxd cloud machine instead of on your machine.
- [Smol Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/smol-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a smolvm microVM on your own machine, isolated from your files and processes.
- [BoxLite Sandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/boxlite-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a BoxLite micro-VM on your own machine, isolated from your files and processes.
- [OpenSandbox](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/opensandbox-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a sandbox on your own OpenSandbox server, on Docker or Kubernetes.
- [Docker Container](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/docker-container/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits in a local Docker or Podman container, created on first use.
- [SSH Workspace](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/ssh-workspace/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands and file edits on another machine over SSH, with your own ssh client and configuration.
- [Bubblewrapped Workspace](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/bubblewrap-sandbox/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent's commands in a Linux bubblewrap wrapper on the host they run on, over SSH or locally.

### Tools & Native Abilities

- [MCP Capability](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/mcp/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to local or remote MCP servers with the MCP capability, calling tools from your own process or via provider-native MCP.
- [Image Generation Capability](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/image-generation/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent generate images when it decides to, via the provider's native image tool or a fallback image model or image-capable subagent.
- [File Understanding](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/file-understanding/index.md)

### Integrations

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/integrations/index.md): Pydantic AI Harness capabilities that connect an agent to third-party services: GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, PostHog, Logfire and more.
- [GitHub](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/github/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent GitHub tools through GitHub's hosted MCP server: read and change repositories, issues, and pull requests with per-user tokens.
- [Linear](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/linear/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Linear tools through Linear's hosted MCP server: read and update issues, projects, and comments, with per-user tokens or OAuth.
- [Macroscope](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/macroscope/index.md): Run a local Macroscope code review from a Pydantic AI agent and get structured findings it can verify and fix with its own file and shell tools.
- [LocalStack](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/localstack/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent access to an emulated AWS environment through the AWS CLI, with an optional Docker-managed LocalStack container lifecycle.
- [Google Workspace](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/google-workspace/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, and People tools through Google's hosted MCP servers, with per-user OAuth tokens.
- [Notion](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/notion/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Notion tools through Notion's hosted MCP server: search and edit pages in a workspace, with per-user OAuth access tokens.
- [Slack](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/slack/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Slack tools through Slack's hosted MCP server: read and send messages, browse channels, and edit canvases as a Slack user.
- [Day AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/day-ai/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to Day AI's hosted MCP server to search and update CRM records and meeting context.
- [Grain](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/grain/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to Grain's hosted MCP server to search and read meetings, transcripts, and notes, and to create clips and tag meetings.
- [Pylon](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/pylon/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to Pylon's hosted MCP server to work with support issues, accounts, and contacts.
- [StackOne](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/stackone/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to a user's linked business apps, such as BambooHR, Salesforce, Workday, or Zendesk, and run their actions through StackOne.
- [PostHog](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/posthog/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to PostHog's hosted MCP server to query product analytics and manage feature flags, experiments, and dashboards.
- [Logfire MCP](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/logfire-mcp/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Logfire tools through the hosted Logfire MCP server: query traces and telemetry and manage projects, with per-user API keys.
- [Ordinal](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/ordinal/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to Ordinal's hosted MCP server to draft, schedule, and analyze social posts.

### Web & Research

- [Web Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/web-search/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent web search with the WebSearch capability, using the provider's native search when available and a local fallback such as DuckDuckGo.
- [Web Fetch](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/web-fetch/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent fetch the contents of URLs with the WebFetch capability, using the provider's native web fetch tool or a local fallback on other models.
- [X Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/x-search/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent search X (Twitter) posts with the XSearch capability, natively on xAI models or delegated to an xAI subagent from other models.
- [Exa Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/exa-search/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent Exa web search: relevant excerpts per result, full-page reads, opt-in deep search with cited answers, and Exa Agent research runs.
- [You.com](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/youdotcom/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent You.com web search, page reads, cited answers, and multi-step deep research, including a finance research mode, via the You.com APIs.
- [Keenable Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/keenable-search/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent web research tools backed by the Keenable search API -- excerpted search and full-page retrieval, keyless by default and with no extra to install.
- [Browser Use](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/browser-use/index.md): Hand open-ended web tasks from a Pydantic AI agent to a browser-use agent that drives a real Chromium browser and returns text or validated JSON results.
- [Playwright Browser](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/playwright/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent a real Chromium browser through Playwright to navigate, click, type, read, run JavaScript, and screenshot dynamic or logged-in pages.

### Reasoning, Planning & Delegation

- [Thinking](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/thinking/index.md): Enable thinking and reasoning effort in Pydantic AI with the Thinking capability, or use native settings for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock and more.
- [Planning](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/planning/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent a todo list it plans and updates itself, with subtasks, dependencies, SQLite, Postgres, or Redis storage, and a cache-safe reminder.
- [Subagents](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/subagents/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent delegate tasks to named subagents through one delegate_task tool, with per-subagent budgets, model choice, and Markdown agent files.
- [Peers](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/peers/index.md): Let an agent discover and message other agent sessions without controlling their runs.
- [Dynamic Workflow](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/dynamic-workflow/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI orchestrator agent coordinate subagents by writing one sandboxed Python script: fan out in parallel, chain, vote, and retry in one tool call.
- [Advisor](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/advisor/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent consult a second, often stronger model mid-run, via the provider-native advisor tool on Anthropic or OpenRouter, or a local fallback.
- [Background Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/background-tools/index.md): Run slow Pydantic AI tools in the background so the agent keeps working, then deliver each tool's result to the model as a follow-up message when it finishes.

### Context Management

- [Code Mode](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/code-mode/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent call its tools from one sandboxed Python script (programmatic tool calling) instead of one model round-trip per tool call.
- [IPython Code Mode](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/ipython-code-mode/index.md): Let a local Pydantic AI agent run Python and call its tools from a persistent IPython kernel, with full CPython and any installed package.
- [Tool Bridge](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/tool-bridge/index.md): Keep a Pydantic AI agent's tool list fixed with three dispatcher tools, so the prompt cache holds however many tools sit behind them and however they change mid-run.
- [Tool Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/tool-search/index.md): Let the model discover deferred tools on demand with the Pydantic AI ToolSearch capability, so agents with many tools only pay tokens for the ones they use.
- [Caching](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/caching/index.md): Prompt caching in Pydantic AI: why to add the Caching capability to your agents, how each provider caches, what caching costs, what invalidates a cache, and how to check that it works.
- [Provider-Native Compaction](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/compaction/index.md): Keep long Pydantic AI conversations within the context window using OpenAI or Anthropic native compaction, or trim and summarize message history on any model.
- [Compaction Strategies](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/compaction/index.md): Keep a long Pydantic AI agent run within the context window on any model: clear old tool results, trim, or summarize history, with tiered escalation.
- [Tool Output Limits](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/tool-output-limits/index.md): Keep large tool outputs from filling a Pydantic AI agent's context window: truncate them, spill them to a file the model can page through, or summarize them.
- [Warn On Cache Busts](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/warn-on-cache-busts/index.md): Catch prompt cache busts in Pydantic AI: warn when the cached prefix read back collapses between model requests or turns, unless the provider's cache retention window explains it.
- [Label Cross Model History](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/label-cross-model-history/index.md): Tell a Pydantic AI agent's model when earlier assistant turns in its history came from another model, with an appended instruction that leaves earlier messages and the cached prompt prefix unchanged.

### Knowledge & Memory

- [Memory](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/memory/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent long-term memory across runs: a Markdown notebook it writes and searches, per-user namespaces, and file, SQLite, or Postgres stores.
- [Pixeltable](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/pixeltable/index.md): Give a Pydantic AI agent read-only, allowlisted tools over existing Pixeltable tables and embedding indexes, and keep Harness Memory in a Pixeltable table.
- [Conversation Search](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/conversation-search/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent search its past conversation history, including messages compaction removed from context, with BM25 over Step Persistence snapshots.
- [Skills](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/skills/index.md): Load Agent Skills (SKILL.md files) from the run's workspace into a Pydantic AI agent on demand: the model sees each skill's name and description and loads its instructions when needed.
- [Repo Context](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/repo-context/index.md): Load a repo's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md instruction files into a Pydantic AI agent and inventory its skills, subagents, and hooks under .claude or .agents.
- [Report Stale Files](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/report-stale-files/index.md): Tell a Pydantic AI agent when a workspace file it read or wrote has since changed or been deleted, before it reasons from or edits an out-of-date copy.
- [Pydantic AI Docs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/pydantic-ai-docs/index.md): Give an agent a tool that locates and returns Pydantic AI documentation on demand instead of preloading it into the system prompt.
- [Current Time](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/current-time/index.md): Tell a Pydantic AI agent today's date, or the current hour, in a time zone you pick, without breaking the prompt cache.

### Control & Safety

- [Guardrails](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/guardrails/index.md): Add input, output, and tool call guardrails to a Pydantic AI agent: block, redact, retry, or require approval, with built-in secret and PII detectors.
- [Goal](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/goal/index.md): Keep an unattended Pydantic AI agent working until a caller-defined completion check accepts its final answer.
- [Prompt Injection Defender](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/prompt-injection-defender/index.md): Scan a Pydantic AI agent's tool results (emails, tickets, web pages) for indirect prompt injection with StackOne Defender, and optionally block risky ones.
- [Artifact Scanning](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/artifact-scanning/index.md): Scan a Pydantic AI agent's memory files and skills for prompt injection, credential exfiltration, and hidden content before they are stored or loaded.
- [Spend Limits](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/spend/index.md): Set daily, monthly, or per-tenant USD and token budgets for a Pydantic AI agent, track LLM cost per response, and stop requests once a budget is spent.
- [Handle Deferred Tool Calls](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/handle-deferred-tool-calls/index.md): Resolve deferred tool calls inside a Pydantic AI run with HandleDeferredToolCalls: approve, deny or answer them from a handler, or hand a resume token to a person and wait in process or suspended and recorded by a durable engine such as AWS Lambda durable functions.
- [Ask User](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/ask-user/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent ask the user clarifying multiple-choice questions mid-run and wait for answers, from a terminal, web UI, or test answerer you supply.
- [Deny Unanswered](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/deny-unanswered/index.md): Deny approval-required calls and unanswered AskUser questions with readable results, so an unattended run finishes instead of pausing on deferred calls.
- [System Reminders](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/system-reminders/index.md): Re-inject reminders into a long Pydantic AI agent run on a cadence or condition to counter instruction fade, without breaking the prompt cache.
- [Detect Loops](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/detect-loops/index.md): Stop a Pydantic AI agent that repeats the same tool calls or responses, or repeats itself within a streaming response, without making progress: nudge it to change approach, raise an error, or call your own handler.
- [Report Tool Errors](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/report-tool-errors/index.md): Send an exception a Pydantic AI tool raises back to the model as a failed tool result, so the run continues instead of ending.
- [Tool Budgets](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/tool-budgets/index.md): Cap how many times a Pydantic AI agent can call each tool, or any tool, in a run, and refuse exact repeats, with a tool result the model can act on instead of an exception.
- [Report Remaining Budget](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/report-remaining-budget/index.md): Tell a Pydantic AI agent's model, on every request, how many requests, tool calls, tokens and dollars its usage limits and spend budgets have left.
- [Trajectory Judge](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/trajectory-judge/index.md): Use an LLM judge to review a live Pydantic AI agent run every N model requests and steer it back on course mid-run when it drifts from the task.
- [Refine Output](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/refine-output/index.md): Have a Pydantic AI agent review and revise its answer before the run ends, for a set number of rounds.
- [Require Verification](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/require-verification/index.md): Send a Pydantic AI coding agent back to run its tests, lint, type checks, or build when it tries to finish after editing code without a passing check.
- [Wrap Up At Limits](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/wrap-up-at-limits/index.md): End a Pydantic AI agent run with a final answer, instead of `UsageLimitExceeded`, when a usage limit would stop it.
- [Tool Call Judge](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/tool-call-judge/index.md): Ask a second model whether a tool call may run, and block it before the tool function executes.
- [Approval Reviewer](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/approval-reviewer/index.md): Let a second model approve the low-risk tool calls that need approval, and leave the rest to a person.
- [Permissions](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/permissions/index.md): Ask a person before the agent writes files or runs commands, by permission mode and rules.

### Self-Extension

- [Runtime Capability Creation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/capability-creation/index.md): Let a Pydantic AI agent write its own capabilities (tools, hooks, instructions) as Python during a run, validate them, and load them on the next run.

### Execution Runtime

- [Instrumentation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/instrumentation/index.md): Trace Pydantic AI agent runs, model requests and tool calls with OpenTelemetry using the Instrumentation capability, following the GenAI semantic conventions.
- [Step Persistence](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/step-persistence/index.md): Save Pydantic AI agent run snapshots to memory, files, SQLite, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL so you can resume or fork a run after a crash, with a ledger of tool side effects.
- [Render Workflows](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/render-workflows/index.md): Run agents in the background with separate retry, timeout, and compute settings for model requests and tools.
- [Media Stores](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/media/index.md): Store large images, audio, and text from Pydantic AI message history in content-addressed disk, SQLite, S3, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL stores to keep run snapshots small.
- [Managed Prompt](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/managed-prompt/index.md): Back a Pydantic AI agent's instructions with a Logfire-managed prompt so you can version, label, and roll it out without redeploying.
- [Repair Tool Arguments](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/repair-tool-arguments/index.md): Fix malformed JSON tool call arguments from the model, such as trailing commas, single quotes, or truncated JSON, before Pydantic AI validates them.
- [Thread Executor](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/thread-executor/index.md): Run sync tools and callbacks on your own thread pool with the Pydantic AI UseThreadExecutor capability, so long-running servers do not accumulate threads.

### Loop Customization

- [Model Router](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/model-router/index.md): Choose an agent's model from a named menu using another Pydantic AI model.
- [Select Model](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/select-model/index.md): Route each Pydantic AI run or step to a different model, chosen from dependencies, message history or usage, with the SelectModel capability.
- [Model Fallback](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/model-fallback/index.md): Fall back to other models when a Pydantic AI model request fails or its response is rejected, with the ModelFallback capability.
- [Retry On Model Errors](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/retry-on-model-errors/index.md): Retry the same model when a Pydantic AI model request fails with a transient error, with the RetryOnModelErrors capability.
- [Resolve Model ID](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/resolve-model-id/index.md): Map custom model names to Pydantic AI models with ResolveModelId, using run dependencies for per-user API keys, per-tenant providers or model registries.
- [Prepare Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/prepare-tools/index.md): Hide, filter or modify the tools the model sees on each step of a Pydantic AI run with the PrepareTools and PrepareOutputTools capabilities.
- [Prefix Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/prefix-tools/index.md): Namespace a capability's tool names with the Pydantic AI PrefixTools capability to avoid conflicts when composing capabilities with overlapping tool names.
- [Include Tool Return Schemas](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/include-tool-return-schemas/index.md): Send tool return type schemas to the model with the Pydantic AI IncludeToolReturnSchemas capability, natively where supported or in the tool description.
- [Set Tool Metadata](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/set-tool-metadata/index.md): Tag selected tools with metadata key-value pairs using the Pydantic AI SetToolMetadata capability, for other capabilities or custom logic to inspect.
- [Raise Content Filter Error](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/raise-content-filter-error/index.md): Treat any model response stopped by a provider content filter as a ContentFilterError in Pydantic AI, even when partial or refusal text comes back.
- [Reinject System Prompt](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/reinject-system-prompt/index.md): Make sure a Pydantic AI agent's system prompt is always sent, even when message history from a UI or database has dropped it, with ReinjectSystemPrompt.
- [Process History](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/process-history/index.md): Trim, redact or summarize the message history before each model request in a Pydantic AI run by wrapping a history processor in the ProcessHistory capability.
- [Process Event Stream](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/process-event-stream/index.md): Forward a Pydantic AI agent's model streaming and tool execution events to your own handler with the ProcessEventStream capability, even from agent.run().
- [Harness Examples](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/examples/index.md): Example Pydantic AI Harness agents to read and copy: a coding agent built on `Coder` and a web research agent built from the blocks that make up `Researcher`.
- [Third-Party Capabilities](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/third-party/index.md): Find community capability packages for Pydantic AI, covering Agent Skills, SQL analytics and RAG.

## Realtime (speech-to-speech)

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/overview/index.md): Build voice agents with Pydantic AI realtime: live speech-to-speech conversations over the OpenAI Realtime API, Gemini Live, xAI, Azure, Eleven Realtime and ElevenLabs Agents, with your tools.
- [Audio, Images, and Transcripts](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/audio/index.md): Stream PCM microphone audio, text and images into a Pydantic AI realtime session, play back the spoken reply, and show live captions and input transcription.
- [Events](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/events/index.md): Handle the Pydantic AI realtime session event stream: content parts, tool activity, turn boundaries, reconnects and recoverable errors, as typed events.
- [Turns and Interruptions](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/turns/index.md): Control turn-taking in Pydantic AI realtime voice agents: voice activity detection (VAD), barge-in when the user talks over the model, and push-to-talk.
- [Tools](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/tools/index.md): Give Pydantic AI realtime voice agents tools that run on your backend, with argument validation, retries, concurrent execution and recorded tool-call messages.
- [Capabilities and Hooks](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/capabilities/index.md): See which Pydantic AI capabilities and hooks run in a realtime voice session, which do not, and how tools and hooks reach the live session through RunContext.
- [History and Handoff](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/history/index.md): Start Pydantic AI voice sessions from earlier text or voice history, continue them later, or hand the conversation to a text model for summaries and extraction.
- [Deployment](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/deployment/index.md): Deploy a Pydantic AI realtime voice agent: connect browsers and phone calls via WebRTC, a WebSocket relay or a Twilio bridge, and host the long-lived sessions on your server.
- [Connection Lifecycle](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/lifecycle/index.md): Manage a Pydantic AI realtime session's connection: reconnect after drops and session limits, hang up on idle timeouts, and handle realtime errors.
- [Usage and Observability](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/observability/index.md): Track usage and cost of Pydantic AI realtime voice sessions, cap them with usage limits, and trace them with OpenTelemetry and Pydantic Logfire.
- [Troubleshooting](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/troubleshooting/index.md): Fix common Pydantic AI realtime voice problems: no audio, a model that never replies or answers twice, echo cutoffs, stalled tools, lost reconnects.
- [OpenAI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/openai/index.md): Use OpenAI's GPT-Live and gpt-realtime voice models with Pydantic AI through OpenAILiveModel and OpenAIRealtimeModel: setup, model routing, delegation, voices, VAD settings, reasoning and browser WebRTC.
- [Azure](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/azure/index.md): Run Pydantic AI realtime voice agents on Azure OpenAI or Azure AI Voice Live with AzureRealtimeModel: deployment names, transcription, Entra ID auth and WebRTC.
- [Google Gemini](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/gemini/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to Gemini Live on the Gemini API or Vertex AI with GoogleRealtimeModel: native audio, live video, Google Search and settings.
- [xAI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/xai/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to xAI Grok Voice with XaiRealtimeModel: setup, grok-voice model names, voices, turn detection, reasoning and reconnects.
- [ElevenLabs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/realtime/elevenlabs/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to ElevenLabs: Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models with ElevenLabsRealtimeModel, or a hosted ElevenLabs agent with ElevenLabsAgentsRealtimeModel.

## Interfaces

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/interfaces/index.md): Run the same Pydantic AI agent headless, in a terminal, behind a web UI or your own frontend, in an editor, over voice, or as a server for other agents.
- [Web Chat UI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/web/index.md): Chat with your Pydantic AI agents in a browser using the built-in web chat UI, launched from the clai CLI or served from your own Python application.

### UI Event Streams

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/integrations/ui/overview/index.md): Connect a Pydantic AI agent to a chat frontend with UI event stream protocols such as AG-UI and the Vercel AI SDK, served from Starlette or FastAPI.
- [AG-UI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/integrations/ui/ag-ui/index.md): Serve Pydantic AI agents to CopilotKit and other AG-UI frontends, with streamed events, frontend tools, shared state, tool approval interrupts and Slack bots.
- [Vercel AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/integrations/ui/vercel-ai/index.md): Stream Pydantic AI agent runs to frontends built with Vercel AI SDK UI hooks like useChat, using the Vercel AI Data Stream Protocol adapter.
- [Command Line Interface (CLI)](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/integrations/cli/index.md): Chat with LLMs from your terminal using clai, the Pydantic AI command line interface, or serve your own Pydantic AI agents in a browser chat UI.
- [GitHub Agentic Workflows](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/gh-aw/index.md): Run your own Pydantic AI agent in GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw): headless in GitHub Actions on issues, pull requests, or a schedule, with MCP tools.
- [ACP](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/harness/acp/index.md): Run a Pydantic AI agent inside Zed and other editors over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), with streamed text, diff views, tool approval, and sessions.

## ~Guides

- [Extensibility](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/extensibility/index.md): Extend Pydantic AI with capabilities, custom toolsets, models and agents, publish your own capability packages, and find third-party packages built on them.
- [Image Generation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/image-generation/index.md): Generate and edit images from Python with the Pydantic AI ImageGenerator API, using GPT Image, Gemini and Grok Imagine models from OpenAI, Google and xAI.
- [Embeddings](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/embeddings/index.md): Generate text embeddings with Pydantic AI using OpenAI, Google, Cohere, VoyageAI, Bedrock or local Sentence Transformers, for semantic search and RAG.

## MCP

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/mcp/overview/index.md): Use the Model Context Protocol with Pydantic AI: connect agents to MCP servers as a client, use provider-native MCP tools, or run agents inside an MCP server.
- [Client](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/mcp/client/index.md): Connect Pydantic AI agents to MCP servers over Streamable HTTP, SSE or stdio, load them from config, and use sampling, elicitation, resources and auth.
- [Server](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/mcp/server/index.md): Use Pydantic AI agents inside the tools of your own MCP server, and route their LLM calls back through the connected client with MCP sampling.

## Pydantic Evals

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evals/index.md): Pydantic Evals is a code-first Python framework for evaluating LLM apps and agents: score outputs and tool-call trajectories on datasets or live traffic.

### Getting Started

- [Quick Start](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/getting-started/quick-start/index.md): Install Pydantic Evals and run your first eval in Python: define test cases and evaluators, add an LLM judge or latency check, and print the evaluation report.
- [Core Concepts](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/getting-started/core-concepts/index.md): Learn the core concepts of Pydantic Evals, including datasets, cases, experiments, evaluators and evaluation reports, and how they work together.

### Evaluators

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/overview/index.md): Choose the right Pydantic Evals evaluators for your task, from fast deterministic checks to LLM judges and span-based evaluation, and combine them in a dataset.
- [Built-in Evaluators](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/built-in/index.md): Reference for the evaluators built into Pydantic Evals: exact match, contains, type checks, max duration, LLM judge, G-Eval, span checks and confusion matrices.
- [LLM Judge](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/llm-judge/index.md): Use an LLM as a judge in Pydantic Evals: grade outputs against a rubric with LLMJudge, get pass/fail or scores, pick the judge model and write good rubrics.
- [Third-Party Integrations](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/framework-integrations/index.md): Use scoring libraries such as Ragas and DeepEval inside Pydantic Evals by wrapping their metrics as evaluators, without a hard dependency on any framework.
- [Custom Evaluators](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/custom/index.md): Write custom Pydantic Evals evaluators for domain-specific logic, external integrations or specialized metrics by subclassing Evaluator and defining evaluate.
- [Report Evaluators](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/report-evaluators/index.md): Compute experiment-wide metrics with Pydantic Evals report evaluators: confusion matrices, precision-recall and ROC curves with AUC, accuracy and custom tables.
- [Span-Based](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/span-based/index.md): Evaluate how an AI system behaved, not only what it returned, by querying the OpenTelemetry spans from a run with span-based evaluators in Pydantic Evals.
- [Agentic Evaluators](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/agentic/index.md): Evaluate AI agent tool calls with Pydantic Evals: check the agent called the right tools, in the right order, with the right arguments and within budget.
- [Standard Quality Metrics](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/evaluators/standard-quality-metrics/index.md): Score LLM outputs with G-Eval in Pydantic Evals, plus LLM judge rubrics for RAG faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision and recall, and translation.
- [Online Evaluation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/online-evaluation/index.md): Evaluate Pydantic AI agents and functions in production with Pydantic Evals: score every call or a sample in the background and emit OpenTelemetry events.

### How-To Guides

- [Logfire Integration](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/logfire-integration/index.md): Send Pydantic Evals experiments to Pydantic Logfire to view results, inspect each case and its full trace, and compare evaluation runs over time.
- [Dataset Management](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/dataset-management/index.md): Build Pydantic Evals datasets in Python or YAML and JSON files, add cases as you find bugs, and generate synthetic test cases from a typed schema with an LLM.
- [Dataset Serialization](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/dataset-serialization/index.md): Save and load Pydantic Evals datasets as YAML or JSON files, load custom evaluators with custom_evaluator_types, and get IDE autocomplete from a JSON Schema.
- [Concurrency & Performance](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/concurrency/index.md): Control how many Pydantic Evals cases run in parallel with max_concurrency, to balance evaluation throughput against provider rate limits and resource use.
- [Multi-Run Evaluation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/multi-run/index.md): Run each Pydantic Evals case several times with the repeat parameter to measure the variability of a non-deterministic LLM system and average scores per case.
- [Retry Strategies](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/retry-strategies/index.md): Retry rate-limited or timed-out tasks and LLM judge evaluators in Pydantic Evals, with Tenacity stop conditions and exponential backoff passed to evaluate().
- [Metrics & Attributes](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/metrics-attributes/index.md): Track tokens, cost, API calls and custom metrics per case in Pydantic Evals, check them in evaluators, and tag experiments with model and prompt metadata.
- [Case Lifecycle Hooks](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/how-to/lifecycle/index.md): Control per-case setup, context preparation and teardown in a Pydantic Evals run with CaseLifecycle hooks, such as creating a database for each case.
- [Simple Validation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/evals/examples/simple-validation/index.md): A worked Pydantic Evals example: test a title-case function with deterministic evaluators, save the dataset to YAML, and run the evaluation from pytest in CI.

## Pydantic Graph

- [Overview](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/graph/index.md): Model complex workflows as typed graphs and state machines with pydantic-graph, an async graph library for Python where nodes and edges come from type hints.

### Graph Builder

- [Getting Started](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/builder/index.md): Build typed workflow graphs with the pydantic-graph GraphBuilder API: async steps, conditional branching, parallel fan-out, joins and Mermaid diagrams.
- [Steps](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/builder/steps/index.md): Define steps in a pydantic-graph workflow: async functions that read state, dependencies and inputs from StepContext, plus streaming steps that yield values.
- [Joins & Reducers](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/builder/joins/index.md): Synchronize and aggregate results from parallel paths in a pydantic-graph workflow with join nodes and reducers that combine many inputs into one output.
- [Decisions](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/builder/decisions/index.md): Add conditional branching to a pydantic-graph workflow with decision nodes, routing data on its type or value to the next step in the graph builder API.
- [Parallel Execution](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/graph/builder/parallel/index.md): Run steps in parallel in a pydantic-graph workflow by broadcasting one value to several steps or mapping over a collection, using the graph builder API.

## Examples

- [Setup](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/setup/index.md): Install and run the Pydantic AI examples, from setting model provider environment variables to running each example script with uv or pip.

### Getting Started

- [Pydantic Model](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/getting-started/pydantic-model/index.md): A simple Pydantic AI example that constructs a validated Pydantic model from free-form text input, using structured output with any supported model.
- [Weather Agent](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/getting-started/weather-agent/index.md): A Pydantic AI tool calling example: a weather agent chains geocoding and weather API tools to answer a question, plus a Gradio chat UI for it.

### Conversational Agents

- [Chat App with FastAPI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/conversational-agents/chat-app/index.md): Build a simple chat app with FastAPI and Pydantic AI that stores chat history between requests, serializes messages, and streams responses to the browser.
- [Bank Support](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/conversational-agents/bank-support/index.md): A small but complete Pydantic AI example of a support agent for a bank, using dynamic instructions, structured output and tools.

### Data & Analytics

- [SQL Generation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/data-analytics/sql-gen/index.md): A Pydantic AI text-to-SQL example that turns user requests into PostgreSQL queries, with an output validator that checks each query using EXPLAIN.
- [Data Analyst](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/data-analytics/data-analyst/index.md): A Pydantic AI data analyst agent example that loads a Hugging Face dataset into pandas and queries it with DuckDB SQL, sharing DataFrames between tools in deps.
- [RAG](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/data-analytics/rag/index.md): A Pydantic AI RAG example that answers questions about documentation using vector search with pgvector and OpenAI embeddings, exposed to the agent as a tool.
- [TwelveLabs Video Agent](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/data-analytics/twelvelabs-video-agent/index.md): A Pydantic AI example of a video analyst agent that answers questions about a video by calling TwelveLabs Pegasus, a video understanding model, as a tool.

### Streaming

- [Stream Markdown](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/streaming/stream-markdown/index.md): A Pydantic AI example that streams Markdown from an agent and highlights it in the terminal with the rich library, running with OpenAI and Gemini models.
- [Stream Whales](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/streaming/stream-whales/index.md): A Pydantic AI example that streams structured output about whales, validating the data as it arrives and displaying it as a live table with rich.
- [Cancel and Resume](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/streaming/cancellation/index.md): A Pydantic AI example that cancels a streaming agent run from an interactive terminal and resumes the conversation with the history preserved before cancellation.

### Realtime

- [Voice Assistant](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/realtime/realtime-voice/index.md): A Pydantic AI voice assistant example that streams your microphone to OpenAI's gpt-realtime model, calls tools mid-conversation and supports barge-in.
- [Text to Audio](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/realtime/realtime-text-to-audio/index.md): The smallest Pydantic AI realtime example: send text to OpenAI's gpt-realtime model, stream the spoken reply and save it as a WAV file, no microphone needed.
- [Agent Handoff](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/realtime/realtime-handoff/index.md): A Pydantic AI example where a realtime voice model runs a support call, then hands its message history to a regular agent for structured output.
- [Camera Agent](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/realtime/realtime-camera/index.md): A Pydantic AI realtime camera example that streams mic audio and webcam frames to Gemini Live or OpenAI Realtime, with web search and spoken, captioned answers.
- [Browser WebRTC](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/realtime/realtime-webrtc/index.md): A Pydantic AI browser voice agent example: audio goes to OpenAI or Azure Realtime over WebRTC while a server sideband runs tools and keeps the API key private.

### Complex Workflows

- [Flight Booking](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/complex-workflows/flight-booking/index.md): A multi-agent Pydantic AI example: a flight search agent delegates extraction to a second agent, then hands off to a third that parses the user's seat choice.
- [Medical Agent Delegation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/complex-workflows/medical-agent-delegation/index.md): A multi-agent Pydantic AI example where a medical triage agent delegates to specialist agents through tools and combines their structured reports.
- [Business Applications](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/slack-lead-qualifier/index.md): Build and deploy a Pydantic AI agent on Modal that researches new Slack community members, qualifies them as leads, and posts daily summaries to Slack.
- [UI Examples](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/examples/ag-ui/index.md): Run Pydantic AI agents in the AG-UI Dojo example app to see the AG-UI protocol in action, with tools, shared state and human-in-the-loop interactions.

- [Migrate to Pydantic AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/comparisons/migrate-from-other-frameworks/index.md): Migrate an agent app from LangChain, LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Mastra and other frameworks to Pydantic AI with bundled coding agent skills.

## Project

- [Contributing](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/project/contributing/index.md): How to contribute to Pydantic AI: agree an approach before opening a PR, what to expect in review, dev setup and tests, and rules for adding model providers.
- [Upgrade Guide](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/project/changelog/index.md): Pydantic AI upgrade guide and changelog: the breaking changes in each release, how to install V2, and the recommended path to migrate your code from V1.
- [V1 → V2 Migration Map](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/overview/migration/index.md): Migrate Pydantic AI V1 code to V2: a lookup table of renamed and removed APIs, packaging changes and default behavior changes, alongside the full Upgrade Guide.
- [Version Policy](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/project/version-policy/index.md): Pydantic AI's version policy: no intentional breaking changes in minor releases, how deprecations work, and when the next major version can ship after V2.
